target_customer: Women fans of college, NBA and MLS teams buying licensed apparel
problem: Few fashionable women's options existed in college-licensed apparel; students were cutting up team T-shirts.
business_model: Direct and wholesale e-commerce apparel under league and university licenses

technical_complexity.rationale: Apparel e-commerce; difficulty is licensing and supply chain, not software.

defensibility.rationale: 350+ licenses including NBA and MLS and university bookstore access are hard to assemble, though not exclusive.

market_need_then: Founders observed students modifying men's cut team apparel; licensors initially resisted, so they started with school colors.
outcome_analysis: Hype and Vice is active with 55 staff and over 350 licenses including NBA and MLS, after a reported 1.5 million dollar seed around the Summer 2019 batch. Success rests on founders who saw an underserved women's segment and on licensing relationships and campus bookstore distribution, though revenue and later funding are not public.
notes: Seed $1.5M, investors from search summary attributing to Forbes (not fetched); round date unknown. $15M valuation is a single USC write-up claim, undated ('end of YC'). CB Insights shows $1.65M total. Founding year conflicts: 2015 (company/USC) vs 2016 (YC). $10K early money from Mike Lee not recorded as a round. Competitors not sourced.
